source.text: Ἄκουε νῦν περὶ τῶν λίθων τῶν ὑπαγόντων εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομήν. οἱ μὲν οὖν λίθοι οἱ τετράγωνοι καὶ λευκοὶ καὶ συμφωνοῦντες ταῖς ἁρμογαῖς αὐτῶν, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ ἐπίσκοποι καὶ διδάσκαλοι καὶ διάκονοι οἱ πορευθέντες κατὰ τὴν σεμνότητα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐπισκοπήσαντες καὶ διδάξαντες καὶ διακονήσαντες ἁγνῶς καὶ σεμνῶς τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς τοῦ Θεοῦ, οἱ μὲν κεκοιμημένοι, οἱ δὲ ἔτι ὄντες· καὶ πάντοτε ἑαυτοῖς συμφωνήσαντες καὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς εἰρήνην ἔσχον καὶ ἀλλήλων ἤκουον· διὰ τοῦτο ἐν τῇ οἰκοδομῇ τοῦ πύργου συμφωνοῦσιν αἱ ἁρμογαὶ αὐτῶν. 2. Οἱ δὲ ἐκ τοῦ βυθοῦ ἑλκόμενοι καὶ ἐπιτιθέμενοι εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν καὶ συμφωνοῦντες ταῖς ἁρμογαῖς αὐτῶν μετὰ τῶν ἑτέρων λίθων τῶν ἤδη ᾠκοδομημένων τίνες εἰσίν; Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ παθόντες ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Κυρίου. 3. Τοὺς δὲ ἑτέρους λίθους τοὺς φερομένους ἀπὸ τῆς ξηρᾶς θέλω γνῶναι τίνες εἰσίν, κυρία. ἔφη· Τοὺς μὲν εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν ὑπάγοντας καὶ μὴ λατομουμένους, τούτους ὁ Κύριος ἐδοκίμασεν, ὅτι ἐπορεύθησαν ἐν τῇ εὐθύτητι τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ κατωρθώσαντο τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ. 4. Οἱ δὲ ἀγόμενοι καὶ τιθέμενοι εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τίνες εἰσίν; Νέοι εἰσὶν ἐν τῇ πίστει καὶ πιστοί. νουθετοῦνται δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸ ἀγαθοποιεῖν, διότι εὑρέθη ἐν αὐτοῖς πονηρία. 5. Οὓς δὲ ἀπέβαλλον καὶ ἔριττον, τίνες εἰσίν; Οὗτοί εἰσιν ἡμαρτηκότες καὶ θέλοντες μετανοῆσαι· διὰ τοῦτο μακρὰν οὐκ ἀπερίφησαν ἔξω τοῦ πύργου, ὅτι εὔχρηστοι ἔσονται εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομήν, ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν. οἱ οὖν μέλλοντες μετανοεῖν, ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν, ἰσχυροὶ ἔσονται ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἐὰν νῦν μετανοήσωσιν ἐν ᾧ οἰκοδομεῖται ὁ πύργος. ἐὰν δὲ τελεσθῇ ἡ οἰκοδομή, οὐκέτι ἔχουσιν τόπον, ἀλλʼ ἔσονται ἔκβολοι. μόνον δὲ τοῦτο ἔχουσιν, παρὰ τῷ πύργῳ κεῖσθαι.

translation.text:
“Listen now about the stones that go into the building. The stones, then, that are square and white and that fit together at their joints [a]—these are the apostles and bishops [b] and teachers and deacons [c], who walked in the reverent dignity of God [d] and who oversaw and taught and served God’s elect with purity and reverence [e]—some have fallen asleep [f], and some are still alive. They were always in agreement with one another, had peace among themselves, and listened to each other; for this reason their joints fit in the building of the tower.

“And the ones drawn up from the deep [g] and set into the building and fitting together at their joints with the other stones already built—who are they?” “These are the ones who suffered on account of the name of the Lord [h].”

“I want to know who the other stones are that are being carried from the dry land [i], lady.” She said, “Those that go into the building without being hewn [j]—the Lord approved these, because they walked in the uprightness of the Lord [k] and accomplished his commandments [l].”

“And the ones being brought and set into the building—who are they?” “They are new in the faith and faithful [m]. But they are being admonished [n] by the angels to do good, because evil was found in them.”

“And those whom they were casting away and throwing aside [o]—who are they?” “These are people who have sinned and want to repent[t] [p]. For this reason they were not flung far away outside the tower, because they will be useful for the building [q], if they repent. Therefore those who are going to repent—if they repent—will be strong in the faith, if they repent now, while the tower is being built. But if the building is completed, they no longer have a place, but will be cast out [r]. But they have only this: to lie beside the tower [s].”

translation.text:
“Listen now about the stones that go into the building. The stones[t], then, that are square and white and that fit together at their joints [a]—these are the apostles and bishops [b] and teachers and deacons [c], who walked in the reverent dignity of God [d] and who oversaw and taught and served God’s elect with purity and reverence [e]—some have fallen asleep [f], and some are still alive. They were always in agreement with one another, had peace among themselves, and listened to each other; for this reason their joints fit in the building of the tower.

“And the ones drawn up from the deep [g] and set into the building and fitting together at their joints with the other stones already built—who are they?” “These are the ones who suffered on account of the name of the Lord [h].”

“I want to know who the other stones are that are being carried from the dry land [i], lady.” She said, “Those that go into the building without being hewn [j]—the Lord approved these, because they walked in the uprightness of the Lord [k] and kept his commandments [l].”

“And the ones being brought and set into the building—who are they?” “They are new in the faith and faithful [m]. But they are being admonished [n] by the angels to do good, because evil was found in them.”

“And those whom they were casting away and throwing aside [o]—who are they?” “These are people who have sinned and want to repent [p]. For this reason they were not flung far away outside the tower, because they will be useful for the building [q], if they repent. Therefore those who are going to repent—if they repent—will be strong in the faith, if they repent now, while the tower is being built. But if the building is completed, they no longer have a place, but will be cast out [r]. But they have only this: to lie beside the tower [s].”

footnotes.text: Greek ἁρμογαί: the joinings where stones meet; alternatives include “joinings” or “fittings.”
ἐπίσκοποι can be rendered “overseers,” but here “bishops” preserves the second‑century office title.
διάκονοι may be translated “ministers”; we retain “deacons” as an office term.
σεμνότης: “reverent dignity,” also “gravity” or “solemnity.” The phrase points to God as the standard of conduct.
τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς: “the elect,” i.e., God’s chosen people.
“Have fallen asleep” is a customary early-Christian euphemism for death.
“The deep” (βυθός) evokes being drawn up from the depth (likely of the sea) in the tower‑building vision.
“Suffered on account of the name of the Lord” alludes to persecution for fidelity to the Lord; compare early martyr traditions.
“Dry land” (ξηρά) contrasts with the sea imagery; stones from land represent another class within the allegory.
μὴ λατομουμένους: “without being hewn,” i.e., not needing to be cut or dressed to fit.
εὐθύτης: “uprightness” (moral straightness).
κατωρθόω: “accomplish,” also “set right” or “carry out.”
πιστοί can mean “faithful” or “believers.” We choose “faithful” to keep the moral nuance.
νουθετέω: “admonish,” with the sense of corrective instruction.
Text reads ἔριττον; many witnesses reflect ἔρριπτον (“they were throwing”). The sense is removal/discarding.
μετανοεῖν: in specific-sin contexts we render “repent.” Some contexts permit “change one’s mind.”
εὔχρηστοι: “useful,” also “serviceable, fit for use.”
ἔκβολοι: “cast out,” also “expelled” or “thrown out.”
“To lie beside the tower” signals a liminal, excluded status in the allegory—near yet not incorporated.
Or 'that match their joints'.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally excellent, capturing the allegorical and moral tone of Hermas well. A few minor adjustments were made to restore missing conjunctions (οὖν, δὲ), ensure consistency in the metaphor of 'walking' for moral conduct, clarify the dative object of service, and provide a more literal rendering of the final clause.
issues_found: Missing translation of the inferential particle 'οὖν' in 'οἱ μὲν οὖν λίθοι' (The stones, then...).
The participle 'πορευθέντες' was translated as 'went', but 'walked' is the standard idiom for moral conduct and maintains consistency with the translation of 'ἐπορεύθησαν' later in the section.

The phrase 'served with purity and reverence for God’s elect' ambiguously implies reverence *for* the elect. Reordering to 'served God’s elect with purity and reverence' clarifies that 'τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς' is the dative object of 'διακονήσαντες'.
Missing translation of the contrastive 'δὲ' in 'νουθετοῦνται δὲ' (But they are being admonished...).
The phrase 'Only this remains for them' is an interpretive expansion of 'μόνον δὲ τοῦτο ἔχουσιν', which literally means 'But they have only this'.

translation.text: “And those whom they were casting away and throwing aside—who are they?” “These are people who have sinned and want to repent[a]. For this reason they were not flung far away outside the tower, because they will be useful for the building, if they repent. Therefore those who are going to repent—if they repent—will be strong in the faith, if they repent now, while the tower is being built. But if the building is completed, they no longer have a place, but will be cast out. But they have only this: to lie beside the tower.”

base_translation.text: “And those whom they were casting away and throwing aside—who are they?” “These are people who have sinned and want to repent. For this reason they were not flung far away outside the tower, because they will be useful for the building, if they repent. Therefore those who are going to repent—if they repent—will be strong in the faith, if they repent now, while the tower is being built. But if the building is completed, they no longer have a place, but will be cast out. But they have only this: to lie beside the tower.”

translation.text:
“And who are the ones they were rejecting and tossing aside?”

“They are people who have sinned and want to repent[a]. They were not thrown far away from the tower, because if they repent, they can still be used in its construction. Those who are going to repent will be strong in the faith if they repent now, while the tower is still being built. Once it is finished, there will be no place for them, and they will be cast out. The only thing left for them is to lie beside the tower.”

spob_revision_history.previous_text:
“And who are the ones they were rejecting and tossing aside?”

“They are people who have sinned and want to repent. They were not thrown far away from the tower because, if they repent, they can still be used in its construction. Those who intend to repent will become strong in the faith—but they must repent now, while the tower is still being built. Once it is finished, there will be no place for them, and they will be cast out. Their one advantage is that they are lying beside the tower.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and preserves the tower image and the urgent, limited opportunity for repentance. However, “one advantage” introduces an unsupported positive evaluation, and the wording around intending and actually repenting should retain the text’s explicit conditional relation. The recommended revision fixes both points without adding doctrinal interpretation.
